title: SCIM reconciliation + tombstone strategy for SSO deprovisioning edge cases
creator: Liam Chen
description: We currently see intermittent SCIM sync divergences between IdPs and Redwood accounts: groups missing membership, users lingering after deprovisioning, and transient 409/429 responses from some enterprise IdPs. This ticket defines and implements a reconciliation pipeline and a tombstone strategy to ensure eventual consistency without causing mass unintended removals. The goal is safe, auditable deprovisioning with clear operator controls and telemetry for fast incident recovery.
acceptance_criteria: Background reconciliation job that detects and repairs user/group drift between SCIM source and Redwood state within a configurable window
Tombstone metadata on deprovisioned accounts allowing safe delayed deletion and automated rollback for false positives
Idempotent reconciliation operations (use of SCIM externalId / idempotency keys) to avoid repeated create/delete churn
Exponential backoff + persistent retry queue for transient SCIM failures; retries surfaced in admin UI and audit logs
Integration with audit logging so every automated reconciliation action records actor, reason, and original IdP change event
Admin Console view with per-tenant last-sync status, tombstoned entity list, and manual reconcile/rollback controls
End-to-end tests (unit + integration) that simulate 409/429 behavior from IdP and verify eventual consistency within SLA
updates: 2026-02-26: Spike completed. Validated approach to use a two-pass reconciliation: detection (fast scan) and repair (rate-limited writes). Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SENG/SCIM+Reconciliation+Spike

2026-03-01: Decided on tombstone model: mark account/group with tombstone=true and record tombstone_reason, tombstone_at; delayed deletion window default 30 days configurable per-tenant. Trade-off: increases storage and one more state to manage vs. safer rollback semantics.

2026-03-03: Implementation started. Added persistent work queue backed by Redis streams to guarantee at-least-once processing and visibility into retry counts. Initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4512

2026-03-06: Design review with PM/Design: UI wireframes reviewed for admin Console reconciliation dashboard. Feedback: expose tenant-level rollback and a search for tombstoned entities. Wireframes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-example

2026-03-09: Security review request opened; concerns raised about tombstone visibility for low-privilege admins. Action: add RBAC v2 permissions scope 'scim.tombstones.read' and 'scim.tombstones.manage'

2026-03-12: QA wrote integration tests that mock IdP 429 responses; current retry logic performs 5 attempts with exponential backoff + jitter then escalates to manual review queue. Observed a failure mode for long-lived duplicate externalId: planning idempotency token change and conflict resolution rule. Tests: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/scim-recon
rollout_plan: Feature-flag initial rollout for 10 pilot tenants (beta) with tombstone window set to 7 days
Monitor sync error rate, corrective actions per tenant; runbook: escalate to SRE on >5% unexpected deletes
Expand to 50% tenants after 2 weeks if no safety incidents; default tombstone window moves to 30 days
Full rollout after security sign-off and post-deployment audit
qa_plan: Unit tests for tombstone CRUD and RBAC enforcement
Integration tests with mocked SCIM server returning 200/409/429/500
Chaos test: simulate IdP mass-delete event and validate tombstone-only path prevents accidental mass-removal
Manual QA for Admin Console flows: reconcile, force-apply, rollback
